To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
institutional ownership exerts a positive effect on the tendency of firms to adopt ISO 14001 only when financial resources available to firms are limited.

(i) institutional investors are more active in their environmental strategy than previously thought, (ii) institutional investors are not only active in developed countries, but they also are active in developing countries, and (iii) the level of activity is not constant but is dependent on the institutional investor's motivations, the firm's characteristics, and the country's characteristics.

institutional ownership has a positive effect on a corporation's propensity to adopt environmental management systems, and this effect is moderated by financial resources and investment opportunities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of institutional shareholders on corporate environmental strategy, and the role of corporate governance mechanisms in moderating this relationship.
how institutional investors can influence corporate environmental strategy in the Egyptian context.
the influence of the financial community on corporate environmental strategy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the relationship between corporate environmental strategy and institutional ownership is contingent on a variety of factors, such as the type and size of institutional ownership, the type of environmental strategy and the country in which the corporation is located.
, in Egypt, the influence of institutional shareholders on corporate environmental strategy depends on the availability of financial resources and investment opportunities.

, in the Egyptian context, institutional shareholders do not always act as passive or active investors, and the influence of institutional investors on a corporation's adoption of environmental standards is moderated by the availability of financial resources and investment opportunities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

institutional investors in developing countries, such as Egypt, are more likely to ask for environmental responsibility as a means to offset their inability in confronting managerial discretionary power, whereas in developed countries, they are more likely to do so to protect their equity values.
institutional investors are likely to be more interested in corporate social responsibility when they are unable to confront managerial discretion.
institutional investors are not a homogeneous group of shareholders and their influence on corporate social responsibility is not uniform.
The main takeaway from our work is that

institutional shareholders can play a positive role in the development of a firm's environmental strategy, particularly when financial resources are abundant and investment opportunities are abundant.
institutional investors in developing countries are not always passive in their actions towards environmental strategy.
institutional investors are not always active in their actions toward corporate environmental strategy, but rather their actions are moderated by their motives.
